{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (Hosting, Support and Interface Licence Agreement with TrueLink)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Subject:** Playbook review findings and recommended positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed EXHIBIT 10.4 against the playbook. The commercial architecture is broadly favourable to us on the points that most often cause trouble: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum-purchase take-or-pay mechanic beyond an exitable monthly minimum, no MFN running against us, no non-solicit, no liquidated damages and no audit right exercisable against us. Termination for convenience sits with us alone (roughly 30–60 days' notice, no exit fee), and auto-renewal is on one-year terms with a 30-day non-renewal window — both at the preferred position. Governing law (California, San Luis Obispo County) sits at the fallback and is acceptable.

The gaps are concentrated in risk allocation and exit. Seven items require action:

- **Limitation of liability (§ 12)** is one-sided — TrueLink is capped at 12 months' hosting and support compensation while our liability, including our broad indemnity under 12(a), is entirely uncapped. This is expressly walk-away territory under the playbook.
- **Post-termination transition and data return** is absent. On exit we would have no contractual right to the return, export or certified deletion of our own hosted data; § 13 instead places the whole migration burden on us.
- **Vendor warranty** is limited to a Y2K date-handling warranty (§ 9), with no professional-services, conformance, malicious-code or compliance warranty and no remedy.
- **Vendor indemnity** (§ 12(b)) covers only TrueLink's own breach; there is no IP infringement indemnity for the Interface or the Hosting/Support Services, while the Client-side indemnity is broad.
- **Insurance** is not addressed anywhere in the document, notwithstanding that TrueLink hosts our Web Site, holds Client Content and transmits data.
- **Assignment (§ 15)** has no M&A successor carve-out for us and an unqualified consent standard, so TrueLink could block a corporate transaction at will.
- **Ownership (§ 2(d)) and licence scope (§ 2(a))** do not vest us with ownership of Support Services work product or expressly reserve our borrower and loan data, and the licence does not reach our affiliates or contractors.

Two of the drafted redlines (limitation of liability and transition assistance) did not clear verification and need manual drafting before they go out; three others (warranty, indemnity, insurance, assignment, IP, licence scope) were repaired and are ready for review.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Vendor capped at 12 months' fees; our liability uncapped. Walk-away. No consequential-damages exclusion or Excluded Claims. *Redline verification: failed — redraft manually.* |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No data return, migration assistance or certified deletion; § 13 puts the migration burden on us. *Redline verification: failed — redraft manually.* |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only a Y2K warranty (§ 9); § 3 obligations are "reasonable commercial efforts" with no remedy. Disclaimer at p0076 is acceptable as qualified. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 12(b) covers TrueLink breach only; no IP infringement indemnity. Client indemnity in 12(a) is broad. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance provision anywhere; vendor processes our data. Walk-away case under the rule. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 15: no successor/M&A carve-out for us; unqualified consent standard. No CoC-triggered vendor termination (not walk-away). |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 2 LICENSE. | No Client ownership of § 4 Support Services work product; no express reservation of borrower/loan data. § 8(d) Credit Data bargain left intact. |
| Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 LICENSE. | Grant runs to Client only; no affiliates or contractors; no successor-transfer carve-out in § 15. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | Non-exclusive; § 2(a) confirms we may acquire, develop or licence competing products. § 3(i) is narrow and self-triggered. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | None. § 14 exit costs roughly one month's fees, inside the fallback. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | None; better than preferred. Separate Non-Competition Agreement noted for diligence. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 14 gives us a unilateral at-will exit with no fee; TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No audit right against us; verification rights run in our favour under §§ 5–6. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | § 12 INDEMNITY. | §§ 26–27: California law, San Luis Obispo County. At fallback; no arbitration. County-level venue noted only. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | Only MFN language runs in our favour (hosting rates capped at best-customer rates). |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant (fallback) | § 5 COMPENSATION. | § 5a monthly minimum, but 12-month term and § 14 exit; no shortfall or take-or-pay. Minimum amounts left blank. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | § 7 UNSOLICITED COMMERCIAL E-MAIL. | No non-solicit or no-hire binding us. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 13: one-year renewals, 30 days' notice — both at preferred. No reminder or uplift cap (noted only). |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Uncapped Customer liability against a capped Vendor (§ 12).** The playbook treats this as walk-away. We need a mutual, agreement-wide cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, the standard uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirmation that our payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.
2. **No insurance from a vendor that processes our data (§§ 13–30).** TrueLink hosts our Web Site, holds Client Content and transmits data through the Interface; the absence of any coverage requirement is the rule's walk-away case. Preferred: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M available.
3. **No exit or data-return right (risks walk-away).** Absent a transition provision we would have no contractual claim to our own hosted data, borrower and loan records on termination. Preferred: six months' assistance at then-current rates, return within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter; fallback 90 days' assistance with export within 30 days.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Redraft the two failed redlines manually** — the mutual limitation of liability (§ 12) and the transition assistance / data return / certified deletion insertion at § 14 — before the markup goes to TrueLink. These are our two lead asks.
2. **Confirm the repaired redlines** for warranty (after p0060), TrueLink IP indemnity with standard exclusions, remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap, new Section 31 insurance, § 15 assignment (affiliate and M&A successor carve-out, reasonableness, competitor bar, CoC not an assignment), Client ownership of work product with licence-back and no joint ownership, and licence extension to affiliates and contractors.
3. **Close the blank commercial terms.** The § 5a minimum monthly fees are left as "$____" and must be set at or below expected usage. Note also that § 6 excludes the monthly minimums from our supporting-documentation and dispute rights.
4. **Obtain and review the separate Non-Competition Agreement** cross-referenced at § 8(d), including for any personnel restrictions; it sits outside this document and was not reviewed here.
5. **Negotiation sequencing.** Lead with the mutual cap, insurance and data-return/exit package as linked asks; the warranty and IP indemnity are the next tier. Governing law (California, San Luis Obispo County) and the § 5a minimum both sit at the fallback and we do not intend to trade for them.
"}
